K01Compliance switched on · empty
OPENFold compliance inspections into a routine service with a Term trigger? A compliance inspection carries four rules a trigger alone would not: it can never be snoozed, it absorbs nothing and is absorbed by nothing in the routine ladder, its certification date is required, and it holds certificate records with type-labelled numbers and optional files. Folding it in means carrying all four on the Term trigger.

Edited where customers are editedA toggle on the customer info card, below IBS, with a tooltip saying it covers every asset the customer owns. The edit dialog carries the same field as a checkbox in its trailing row — specified in the PRD, not drawn. No settings card, no settings tab, no preferences page.
One field, two placesThe enrolment modal shows the current value and offers the change in place. Card, dialog and modal all write the same boolean on the customer.
On the customer, not the assetA fleet is one relationship. Consent given once covers every unit the customer owns, including units enrolled later.
Off does not stop trackingEvery due date, every status and every worklist row stays exactly as it was. Only the email stops.
Default onDecided 16 September: every customer starts on. A shop switches individual customers off on the record. There is no bulk action and no turn-everyone-on button.
Permission follows the customerEditing this field follows editing a customer. It is not financial data, so it does not sit behind the AP/AR visibility gate the way PO is required does.
No unsubscribe in the emailConsent is managed here, by the shop, on the record. That is why the email carries no unsubscribe link.

Two things record a readingA user changing the mileage on a work order, and the work order being invoiced. Whatever the mileage reads at the moment of invoice becomes the new last recorded reading.
The estimate is replaced, not averagedA recorded reading supersedes whatever was projected. The rate is then measured again from the two most recent recorded readings.
In the shop is not yet recordedA unit on an open work order shows the value the advisor typed, dated today. The invoice is what fixes it.
Everything dependent moves at onceDue points, statuses and the worklist re-resolve on the save, not overnight. The one moment the truck is physically present is now.

The date sits on top, everywhereRoutine and compliance rows read the same way: the date first, its rule underneath. The column is called Comes due, so the date is what answers it.
Every candidate is shownA service with three triggers has three candidate dates. Showing one and hiding two is what made the old cell unreadable.
The earliest is marked, not just sortedFirst says which trigger the system expects to fire. Sorting alone leaves the reader to work it out.
A compliance term is always knownThere is no state where a compliance service has no term, so the cell always resolves. A missing certificate is noted on the row, not in this cell.

5

The spine

Reference
0The spine · objects and where they live
LIVES ON THE ORGANIZATION
Schedulename · an ordered list of services
LIVES ON THE SCHEDULE
Servicename · compliance yes/no · one or more triggers · one interval per trigger · a meter trigger always carries a calendar interval beside it · distance unit · canned lines · a reminder schedule · automatic send: on / off
COMPUTED, NEVER STORED
Due serviceone per service that has come due for an enrolled asset · what appears on the worklist · resets from the invoice date of the work order that completed it
LIVES ON THE ASSET
Enrollmentwhich schedule · baseline readings · stated weekly average · running type
LIVES ON THE ASSET
Compliance recordtype · effective date · expiry month · term · certificate number · exists with or without a schedule · has its own tab on the asset
LIVES ON THE ASSET
Readingvalue · which meter · when it was taken · where it came from
LIVES ON A WORK ORDER
Work-order service linethe service it came from · its own labor and parts · canned lines nested beneath it as sublines
ServiceDue servicea line inside a schedule, and that line coming due for one truck. Two objects, two words.
Compliance recordAsset › Certificatesits own tab on the truck. Remove the schedule and the record stays.
ServiceWork-order service linea service is a work-order line in its own right, not a label on other lines. One four-hour PM-A line, or four canned lines nested beneath it as sublines.

R1The email, as the customer receives it

Sent because Aacrest Works is the contact for these units at Staging Heavy Duty.
One email, every stateA unit can be upcoming, due today and past due at the same moment. Three emails would have an owner opening three messages about one truck.
The wording is fixedIdentical for every shop. Nothing here is editable, which is why there is no settings screen behind it.
It holds for any mixOne row or forty, all past due or all upcoming: the opening line never needs a singular and a plural version.
The state sits on the rowNot in the heading, not in the subject. The table carries it.
No unsubscribeHonouring one properly is consent management, which is its own feature. Consent lives on the customer record instead.
Soon, where a date would be a guessA unit with no basis to estimate from reads Soon rather than a date the shop would be held to.
